name: Token Approval Risk Scanner API
shortDescription: Scan ERC-20 token approvals for unlimited allowances, flagged spenders, and stale grants — with a revoke-priority list.
description: Deterministic scanner for ERC-20 token approvals (allowances). Flags unlimited allowances, flagged/unverified spenders, and stale grants, scores per-approval and portfolio drain exposure (0–100 with low/medium/high/severe bands), and returns a revoke-priority list ranked by risk. It scores the approvals you supply — no chain fetch — so it is advisory, not a verdict on a live wallet. Built for wallet-safety agents, DeFi guardrails, and approval-hygiene workflows. /scan returns per-approval risk and the revoke list; the one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object and prioritized actions. No LLM, nothing stored.
typicalUseCases: Pre-transaction approval hygiene check for a wallet agent
Surfacing unlimited/stale allowances a user should revoke
Feeding approval drain-exposure into a wallet trust verdict
DeFi guardrail before granting or acting on an approval

name: Wallet Risk Bundle API
shortDescription: Fuse address risk, exposure, approvals, reputation, and balance into one composite score, trust tier, and allow/review/block verdict.
description: Deterministic wallet trust/risk fusion layer. Combines the signals an agent has already gathered — address risk, mixer/flagged exposure, token-approval exposure, reputation, and balance context — into a single composite risk score (0–100), a trust tier (trusted/neutral/caution/high_risk), and an allow/review/block verdict. The composite is re-weighted over whichever signals you supply; any omitted signal is returned under missing_sources with a chain_to pointer to the live Orbis API that produces it (wallet-address-risk, token-approval-risk-scanner, wallet-reputation). Hard-block signals (sanctioned address, heavy mixer/flagged exposure) force a block verdict. It scores the signals you pass in — no chain fetch. /assess returns the verdict and per-source contributions; the one-call /lookup adds a reasoning object and prioritized actions. No LLM, nothing stored.
typicalUseCases: Single allow/review/block gate for an autonomous wallet/DeFi agent
Fusing separate risk lookups into one trust verdict before acting
Compliance triage of a counterparty wallet from gathered signals
Routing an agent to fetch only the wallet signals it is still missing
